newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli soldier killed in Hizbollah attack.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier killed in Hizbollah attack.

text.p: One Israeli soldier was killed and three others wounded on Wednesday in the bloodiest guerrilla raid in south Lebanon in seven weeks, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

The fighting on the last active Arab-Israeli warfront came a day after Israel broke ground for the building of homes for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem in a step that drew fire from some European countries, Arab states and anti-Israeli Islamist and Palestinian guerrilla groups.

The Hizbollah guerrillas fired rockets, rocket-propelled grenades and machineguns at the Israeli patrol in Arnoun area on the edge of a border zone that Israel occupies in south Lebanon, the South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia sources said.
"One Israeli soldier was killed and three wounded, two of them seriously, as a result of the assault," one SLA source said. "The wounded soldiers were taken by helicopter to Israel."

The Shi'ite Moslem fighters also rained down mortar bombs at a fortified post held by the Israeli army at Dabsheh near Arnoun and another nearby outpost held by its SLA militia allies at Ali Taher, but no one was hurt, the sources added.

In retaliation, Israeli artillery gunners shelled hills controlled by Hizbollah north of the zone, the SLA sources said. There was no immediate report on casualties in the retaliatory bombardment, which mainly targeted areas facing Arnoun.
Wednesday's casualties raised to six the number of Israeli soldiers killed and 26 wounded in south Lebanon this year. Last year, 27 Israeli soldiers were killed in Lebanon.

The latest attack -- the fourth fatal one in 1997 -- was the bloodiest in south Lebanon since January 30 when three Israeli soldiers were killed and one wounded in a bomb assault carried out by Hizbollah guerrillas.
The pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) claimed responsibility for the attack, which came six days after Lebanon marked the 19th anniversary of Israel's first invasion of south Lebanon in 1978.

In Beirut, a Hizbollah spokesman told Reuters the guerrillas fired at an Israeli patrol in the Arnoun-Zafateh area, hitting a military vehicle and killing or wounding those inside, and also attacked the Ali Taher position.

Hizbollah leads an Islamic Resistance vying to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 SLA militiamen from the 15-km (nine-miles)- deep zone in south Lebanon set up by Israel to stop cross-frontier raids on northern Israel.

In Damascus, three radical Palestinian groups on Wednesday called on Palestinians to launch Jihad (Holy War) and military attacks against Israel to force it to stop building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

The call was made by the Islamic Jihad, the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) and the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine (DFLP). The groups have claimed several attacks in which scores of Israelis were killed.
The Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas, which like Jihad operates in the Israeli-occupied territories, called for a comprehensive programme to confront the Israeli plans.

Syria, Lebanon's main power broker which wields considerable influence with Hizbollah, has accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of bringing the region to the brink of war by building settlements in occupied Arab lands.
